Defining NP functions and noun inflections: NP subject, object, PC; noun head, number and genitive case; dependents characteristic of noun heads.
Personal pronouns function as nouns in NP structure though their case paradigms differ; NP functions beyond complements include modifiers, supplements and vocatives; dummy there is NP.
Bare role NP is licensed as PC but not ordinary referential subject/object; classes common/proper/pronoun and count vs noncount are introduced.
Nominal intermediate category distinguishes internal head from a full NP; United States/Ministry of Defence nominal pre-head modification; two NP/nominal structure trees.
Ultimate head, external determiner function versus determinative lexical class, genitive NP determiners, recursive nominal premodifiers and posthead dependents.
Nominal recursive complements/modifiers versus external NP dependents; predeterminer and peripheral modifier forms and their different phrase positions; two trees.
Full layered NP tree with predeterminer and peripheral adjunct; fused modifier/determiner/predeterminer heads contrasted with genuine ellipsis and hybrid VP-headed NP.
Simple, partitive and special fused-head constructions; subordinate content/infinitival/gerund-participial clauses cannot be relabelled as NPs just for subject use.
Number features in noun, NP, pronoun and verb agreement; countability cardinal numeral diagnostic and chocolate count/noncount semantic polysemy.
Count/noncount alternations per sense include paper, building, study, hair and duty; substances vs heterogeneous aggregate conceptualisations.
Homogeneous water versus heterogeneous crockery; noncount aggregate inventory; serving/variety senses of drinks and food produce licensed count use.
Animal/meat sense shifts, restricted abstract event and result countability, nonce substance coercion of normally count nouns.
Number and countability cross-cut (plural noncount oats), unlike base plurals; cross-language lexicalisation and determiner compatibility.
Determinatives a little/much versus each/every/another select different count senses; exceptional a with knowledge/regard; all singular noncount.
Bare count singular ordinarily requires a determiner, unlike noncount; irregular base plurals (sheep), plural-only bipartite nouns and beginning inflection distinctions.
